instructions: Rinse the 1.5 cups rice in a few changes of water until the water runs mostly clear. Cook it in a rice cooker, or in a covered pot with 1 3/4 cups water over low heat for 18 minutes, then leave it covered off the heat for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, mince the 6 garlic cloves and enough of the ginger to fill 2 tsp. In a large bowl, stir together the 1/4 cup gochujang, 1 tbsp of the gochugaru, the 3 tbsp soy sauce, the 2 tbsp + 2 tsp sugar, the garlic, the ginger, the 2 tsp sesame seeds and the pinch of black pepper. Put the other 1 tbsp gochugaru in a small bowl for the table.

Rinse the 1.75 lbs squid and pat it dry. Cut the bodies into rings about 3/4 inch wide, and cut the tentacles into pieces about the same size. Keep the pieces on the big side. They shrink a lot in the pan.
Add the squid to the sauce bowl and toss until every piece is coated. Leave it there while you cut the vegetables.
Slice the onion. Cut the carrot and the zucchini in half lengthwise, then slice them thinly on an angle into pieces about 2 inches long. Cut 4 of the scallions into 2 inch lengths.

Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat until it's very hot, then add the 2 tbsp vegetable oil. Add the carrot first, then the onion, zucchini and scallions. Stir fry for about 2 minutes, until the edges start to soften but they still have some bite.

Push the vegetables out to the sides of the pan. Add the squid and all of its sauce to the middle. Stir fry for about 2 minutes, until the pieces curl up and turn white all the way through. Don't let it go longer. Overcooked squid turns rubbery.
Toss the squid and vegetables together for about 1 minute, then take the pan off the heat and drizzle over the 2 tbsp sesame oil.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a small splash more soy sauce.
Serve over the rice, with the gochugaru on the side.
method_notes: All three versions read use a gochujang, gochugaru, soy, sugar and garlic sauce, cook over high heat and warn that the squid toughens if it's cooked more than a couple of minutes. Korean Bapsang marinates the squid in the sauce while the vegetables are cut and adds zucchini; Beyond Kimchee fries leek first and reduces the sauce separately, and Kimchi Mari adds cabbage and a little water and cooks the vegetables longer. This one follows Korean Bapsang doubled for 4, uses sugar in place of its corn syrup, and moves half the chili flakes to the table so the pot stays milder.
